segments.speaker: Odessa Pruitt
segments.text: Linden, I need to talk about the man with the rockets.

segments.speaker: Linden Aldous
segments.text: Odessa, there are several men with rockets now. It is a whole aisle.

segments.speaker: Odessa Pruitt
segments.text: Elon Musk, Linden. The man bought Twitter and named it after a letter.

segments.speaker: Linden Aldous
segments.text: X. It is a bold choice. It is the letter you put on a map where the treasure is.

segments.speaker: Odessa Pruitt
segments.text: It is the letter you put on a form when you cannot write your name.

segments.speaker: Linden Aldous
segments.text: I still call it Twitter. Everybody does. It is like calling the bodega by the old owner's name.

segments.speaker: Odessa Pruitt
segments.text: That is respect. The bird earned it. The bird did nothing wrong.

segments.speaker: Linden Aldous
segments.text: In fairness, the man lands rockets backwards. On a boat. I cannot park a bike.

segments.speaker: Odessa Pruitt
segments.text: I will give him the rockets. The rockets are impressive. It is the posting.

segments.speaker: Linden Aldous
segments.text: He does post a lot.

segments.speaker: Odessa Pruitt
segments.text: Linden, he posts like my uncle at a wedding with the microphone. Nobody handed it to him. He just has it.

segments.speaker: Linden Aldous
segments.text: He wants to put a city on Mars.

segments.speaker: Odessa Pruitt
segments.text: We cannot put a working elevator in the Marcy houses and we are doing Mars?

segments.speaker: Linden Aldous
segments.text: Mars has no rent stabilization, Odessa. That is the selling point.

segments.speaker: Odessa Pruitt
segments.text: Mars has no air, Linden. That is the other selling point.

segments.speaker: Pat, the producer
segments.text: A note from the booth. The show has no position on Mars. Mars has not called in.

segments.speaker: Odessa Pruitt
segments.text: Thank you, Pat. And the Tesla. Tell me about the truck.

segments.speaker: Linden Aldous
segments.text: The Cybertruck. It looks like a doorstop that got a lawyer.

segments.speaker: Odessa Pruitt
segments.text: It looks like somebody drew a truck with a ruler during a power outage.

segments.speaker: Linden Aldous
segments.text: I like it. It is honest. It looks the way a parking ticket feels.

segments.speaker: Odessa Pruitt
segments.text: And the self-driving. They have been saying next year since my nephew was in kindergarten. He drives now. Himself.

segments.speaker: Linden Aldous
segments.text: Your nephew is the self-driving car, Odessa.

segments.speaker: Odessa Pruitt
segments.text: My nephew is the only self-driving car I trust, and he still cannot find Halsey Street.

segments.speaker: Linden Aldous
segments.text: Here is my theory. One day he renames the moon. Just X. The moon becomes X.

segments.speaker: Odessa Pruitt
segments.text: Then the moon starts charging eight dollars a month for the blue check.

segments.speaker: Linden Aldous
segments.text: A verified moon. That is a premium tide.

segments.speaker: Odessa Pruitt
segments.text: Linden, that is the dumbest thing you have said this week, and it is only Tuesday.

segments.speaker: Linden Aldous
segments.text: It is Thursday.

segments.speaker: Pat, the producer
segments.text: It is Wednesday. I checked. I am very good at checking.

segments.speaker: Odessa Pruitt
segments.text: Pat, nobody likes that you are good at checking.

segments.speaker: Linden Aldous
segments.text: The phones are open. Today: iPhone or Android. Mac or PC. Pick a side and defend it.

segments.speaker: Odessa Pruitt
segments.text: Keep it clean. Nobody's grandmother has to hear about the charger cable again.

segments.speaker: Linden Aldous
segments.text: First caller, Kenji from Nostrand. You are in The Group Chat.

segments.speaker: Kenji from Nostrand
segments.text: Linden, I have had an Android for eleven years and I am tired of being the green bubble.

segments.speaker: Odessa Pruitt
segments.text: The green bubble. You are the cousin at the cookout nobody wants to text.

segments.speaker: Kenji from Nostrand
segments.text: I am not the problem! My phone folds! It folds in half, like a wallet that knows things!

segments.speaker: Linden Aldous
segments.text: Why does it need to fold, Kenji?

segments.speaker: Kenji from Nostrand
segments.text: Because I can, Linden. Because Google let me. That is called freedom.

segments.speaker: Odessa Pruitt
segments.text: Google lets you do a lot of things. Then Google cancels them.

segments.speaker: Kenji from Nostrand
segments.text: That is true. I had a Google thing. I loved it. They held a funeral. I was not invited.

segments.speaker: Linden Aldous
segments.text: Thank you, Kenji. Next, Brianna from Greene. Brianna, you are nineteen?

segments.speaker: Brianna from Greene
segments.text: Yes. And I need everyone to know an Android is not a phone. It is a calculator with feelings.

segments.speaker: Odessa Pruitt
segments.text: Gen Z has entered the chat. Brianna, what is wrong with the green bubble?

segments.speaker: Brianna from Greene
segments.text: It is giving group project. It is giving a free trial.

segments.speaker: Linden Aldous
segments.text: And what does your iPhone give, Brianna?

segments.speaker: Brianna from Greene
segments.text: It gives a new one every September that looks exactly like the old one, and I buy it, and I feel seen.

segments.speaker: Odessa Pruitt
segments.text: That is the most honest thing anybody has said on this show.

segments.speaker: Brianna from Greene
segments.text: Also I do not answer calls. If you call me, I assume somebody died or you are a scam.

segments.speaker: Linden Aldous
segments.text: Last caller, Dale from Kosciuszko. Dale, you are a Gen X man. What do you use?

segments.speaker: Dale from Kosciuszko
segments.text: A PC I built myself in two thousand and nine. It has eleven fans. It sounds like a small airport.

segments.speaker: Odessa Pruitt
segments.text: Dale, what about a Mac?

segments.speaker: Dale from Kosciuszko
segments.text: A Mac is a very expensive way to not be allowed to open your own computer.

segments.speaker: Brianna from Greene
segments.text: Okay, boomer.

segments.speaker: Dale from Kosciuszko
segments.text: I am not a boomer! I am Gen X! Nobody ever remembers us! That is our whole thing!

segments.speaker: Linden Aldous
segments.text: Dale, how do you text your family?

segments.speaker: Dale from Kosciuszko
segments.text: The family WhatsApp. My mother sends a voice note every morning. It is six minutes long. It is a prayer and a weather report.

segments.speaker: Odessa Pruitt
segments.text: Every family has a WhatsApp group where one uncle forwards the same video of a dog on a skateboard.

segments.speaker: Dale from Kosciuszko
segments.text: That uncle is me, Odessa. And that dog is a hero.

segments.speaker: Linden Aldous
segments.text: So who wins, Odessa? iPhone or Android?

segments.speaker: Odessa Pruitt
segments.text: Nobody wins, Linden. We all pay a thousand dollars to look at the same weather app and complain.

segments.speaker: Pat, the producer
segments.text: For the record, the booth runs on a computer older than Brianna. It is doing its best.

bits.title: The Professor of Things That Are Going On

segments.speaker: Odessa Pruitt
segments.text: Joining us in the studio, a man with tenure at a university that is mostly a laundromat on Fulton.

segments.speaker: Professor Hollis Wexley
segments.text: Professor Hollis Wexley. Department of Things That Are Going On. Thank you, Odessa.

segments.speaker: Linden Aldous
segments.text: Professor, today we want to understand artificial intelligence.

segments.speaker: Professor Hollis Wexley
segments.text: Nobody understands it, Linden. That is why it is worth so much money.

segments.speaker: Odessa Pruitt
segments.text: Start simple. What is Open A I?

segments.speaker: Professor Hollis Wexley
segments.text: Open A I is a company called Open, that you cannot open. It is like a door that is also a wall that is also a subscription.

segments.speaker: Linden Aldous
segments.text: And Sam Altman runs it.

segments.speaker: Professor Hollis Wexley
segments.text: Correct. In twenty twenty-three his own board let him go on a Friday and he was back within the week. My cousin got fired from the deli on Lewis and he is still not back.

segments.speaker: Odessa Pruitt
segments.text: That is the dream, Professor. Fired on Friday, rehired by brunch.

segments.speaker: Professor Hollis Wexley
segments.text: The man raises money the way I raise my voice at the dryer. Constantly, and in public.

segments.speaker: Linden Aldous
segments.text: What does the money buy?

segments.speaker: Professor Hollis Wexley
segments.text: Computer chips. Big buildings full of computer chips. The buildings are so hot they need their own rivers.

segments.speaker: Odessa Pruitt
segments.text: Our building cannot get heat in January and theirs needs a river.

segments.speaker: Professor Hollis Wexley
segments.text: Exactly. The future is warm, Odessa. Just not in your apartment.

segments.speaker: Linden Aldous
segments.text: And Google? Apple? Are they in the race?

segments.speaker: Professor Hollis Wexley
segments.text: Everybody is in the race. Google put a robot answer on top of the search, so now you ask how long to boil an egg and it writes you a poem about eggs.

segments.speaker: Odessa Pruitt
segments.text: And Apple?

segments.speaker: Professor Hollis Wexley
segments.text: Apple is in the race the way my uncle is in a marathon. Walking. Confident. Wearing a very nice watch.

segments.speaker: Linden Aldous
segments.text: Professor, will A I take our jobs?

segments.speaker: Professor Hollis Wexley
segments.text: It will take some jobs. But it cannot take yours, Linden. Nobody knows what yours is.

segments.speaker: Odessa Pruitt
segments.text: Thank you. I have been saying that for years.

segments.speaker: Professor Hollis Wexley
segments.text: Also it cannot hold a ladder. Or wait for a delivery between nine and five. Humanity still has the ladder.

segments.speaker: Linden Aldous
segments.text: And the stock market?

segments.speaker: Professor Hollis Wexley
segments.text: The stock market goes up whenever somebody says A I on a phone call. I said it twice this morning. My cousin's coin went up eleven percent.

segments.speaker: Odessa Pruitt
segments.text: Professor, is any of this real?

segments.speaker: Professor Hollis Wexley
segments.text: Odessa, I teach in a laundromat. I am not under oath.

segments.speaker: Pat, the producer
segments.text: The booth would like to note that Pat is not artificial intelligence. Pat is just quiet.

segments.speaker: Odessa Pruitt
segments.text: Pat, that is exactly what it would say.

segments.speaker: Linden Aldous
segments.text: It is time for the consumer desk, with Gloria Fenn, who is not a lawyer, but who has been very angry in many lobbies.

segments.speaker: Gloria Fenn
segments.text: Thank you, Linden. I have been on hold since the last time I was on this show.

segments.speaker: Odessa Pruitt
segments.text: Gloria, first question. My streaming went up again.

segments.speaker: Gloria Fenn
segments.text: Of course it did. Streaming was sold to us as cheaper than cable. Now you have five of them and together they cost more than cable, plus they put the ads back.

segments.speaker: Linden Aldous
segments.text: And they stopped password sharing.

segments.speaker: Gloria Fenn
segments.text: They stopped password sharing. My nephew had my password for nine years. It was the only thing we shared. Now we do not speak.

segments.speaker: Odessa Pruitt
segments.text: What do we do?

segments.speaker: Gloria Fenn
segments.text: Cancel one every month. Rotate them like tires. Let them miss you.

segments.speaker: Linden Aldous
segments.text: Next. The airlines.

segments.speaker: Gloria Fenn
segments.text: Linden, I flew to Atlanta. The seat was cheap. Then the bag was money. Then the seat next to my own child was money. Then the overhead bin was money.

segments.speaker: Odessa Pruitt
segments.text: The air is still free?

segments.speaker: Gloria Fenn
segments.text: For now, Odessa. For now. Do not give them ideas. Somebody in an office is listening.

segments.speaker: Linden Aldous
segments.text: Concert tickets.

segments.speaker: Gloria Fenn
segments.text: The ticket is a hundred dollars. Then there is a service fee for the service of selling you the ticket. Then a facility fee for the facility you have not entered. Then a fee called convenience. There is nothing convenient.

segments.speaker: Odessa Pruitt
segments.text: And the resale.

segments.speaker: Gloria Fenn
segments.text: You wake up at ten in the morning, it sells out at ten oh one, and by ten oh two a man named Brent is selling it back to you for the price of a used car.

segments.speaker: Linden Aldous
segments.text: Gloria, the tipping screen.

segments.speaker: Gloria Fenn
segments.text: Oh, the tipping screen. I bought a bottle of water from a fridge. I took it out of the fridge myself. The screen turned around and asked for twenty five percent.

segments.speaker: Odessa Pruitt
segments.text: Twenty five percent of what?

segments.speaker: Gloria Fenn
segments.text: Of my dignity, Odessa. And there is a button that says custom, and the cashier watches you press it, and you age a year.

segments.speaker: Linden Aldous
segments.text: And self-checkout.

segments.speaker: Gloria Fenn
segments.text: I scanned my own groceries, bagged my own groceries, and the machine said unexpected item in the bagging area. The unexpected item was me. I work there now, apparently, for free.

segments.speaker: Odessa Pruitt
segments.text: Gloria, any good news?

segments.speaker: Gloria Fenn
segments.text: Yes. Read the receipt. Ask for the fee to come off. Say the word supervisor slowly, like a spell.

segments.speaker: Linden Aldous
segments.text: Gloria Fenn, everybody. Not a lawyer.

segments.speaker: Gloria Fenn
segments.text: Not a lawyer. Still on hold. Thank you.

segments.speaker: Linden Aldous
segments.text: We have to pay the bills. Here are three messages from businesses that may not exist.

segments.speaker: Patience Brothers Investing
segments.text: Do you want to invest like the old man in Omaha?

segments.speaker: Patience Brothers Investing
segments.text: Step one. Buy a good company. Step two. Live in the same house for sixty years. Step three. Do absolutely nothing.

segments.speaker: Patience Brothers Investing
segments.text: Patience Brothers. We are not affiliated with Warren Buffett. He has never heard of us. That is part of the strategy.

segments.speaker: Patience Brothers Investing
segments.text: Results not typical, because you are not him, and you checked your phone during this ad.

segments.speaker: Group Chat Jingle
segments.text: The Group Chat. Ninety-nine point nine.

segments.speaker: The Multiverse Pass
segments.text: Tired of homework before the movies? Get the Multiverse Pass.

segments.speaker: The Multiverse Pass
segments.text: Watch all forty superhero films you need to understand the next one, plus three shows, two cartoons, and a scene after the credits that explains a different scene after different credits.

segments.speaker: The Multiverse Pass
segments.text: The Multiverse Pass. Marvel did not make this ad. Marvel is busy making phase twelve.

segments.speaker: The Multiverse Pass
segments.text: Warning. Side effects include saying, wait, which one is this, in a dark room.

segments.speaker: Group Chat Jingle
segments.text: Everybody is typing.

segments.speaker: Landlord Calm
segments.text: Are you a landlord who feels misunderstood?

segments.speaker: Landlord Calm
segments.text: Try Landlord Calm, a soothing audio track of a tenant saying, no worries, take your time with the heat.

segments.speaker: Landlord Calm
segments.text: Landlord Calm also includes the sound of a radiator working, for landlords who have never heard it.

segments.speaker: Landlord Calm
segments.text: Landlord Calm. The broker fee is included. The broker is also included. He lives in the closet now.

segments.speaker: Pat, the producer
segments.text: All three advertisers are invented. Please do not send them money. They will not know what to do with it.

segments.speaker: Odessa Pruitt
segments.text: Pat, the Patience Brothers would know what to do with it. They would do nothing with it, for sixty years.

segments.speaker: Linden Aldous
segments.text: Odessa, I signed up for the Multiverse Pass during the ad.

segments.speaker: Odessa Pruitt
segments.text: Linden, you have not finished the first movie of the first phase.

segments.speaker: Linden Aldous
segments.text: I am pacing myself. I will be ready for the next one by the time I retire.

segments.speaker: Odessa Pruitt
segments.text: By then the Patience Brothers will own the theater, and Landlord Calm will be the landlord.

segments.speaker: Linden Aldous
segments.text: Listener mail. You write, we read it on air, and nobody learns anything.

segments.speaker: Odessa Pruitt
segments.text: First letter, from a man on Madison Street. Dear Group Chat. Why do women say they are fine when they are not fine?

segments.speaker: Linden Aldous
segments.text: Odessa, I want to take this one.

segments.speaker: Odessa Pruitt
segments.text: Linden, you should not take this one.

segments.speaker: Linden Aldous
segments.text: When a woman says fine, it means the conversation is over, but the meeting is still scheduled.

segments.speaker: Odessa Pruitt
segments.text: And when a man says I will fix it, it means the thing will stay broken until it becomes a family heirloom.

segments.speaker: Linden Aldous
segments.text: That is fair. The shelf in my hallway is an heirloom. My grandson will inherit the wobble.

segments.speaker: Odessa Pruitt
segments.text: Second letter, from a woman on Monroe. Dear Group Chat, why do men need a podcast?

segments.speaker: Linden Aldous
segments.text: Because no one in our lives will listen to us for two hours, so we rent a microphone.

segments.speaker: Odessa Pruitt
segments.text: Thank you for admitting that. And women do not need a podcast, because we have each other's voice notes, and they are longer.

segments.speaker: Linden Aldous
segments.text: So both sides lose.

segments.speaker: Odessa Pruitt
segments.text: Everybody loses, Linden. That is what love is.

segments.speaker: Linden Aldous
segments.text: Next letter. Dear Group Chat, I went on a date and he spent the whole dinner taking pictures of the food for Instagram. The food was cold by the time he let me eat it.

segments.speaker: Odessa Pruitt
segments.text: That is not a date, that is a photo shoot with a side of you.

segments.speaker: Linden Aldous
segments.text: In his defense, the pasta had good lighting.

segments.speaker: Odessa Pruitt
segments.text: Next. Dear Group Chat, my roommate went vegan and now every conversation becomes about it. I asked her the time and she told me cows have friends.

segments.speaker: Linden Aldous
segments.text: Cows do have friends, Odessa.

segments.speaker: Odessa Pruitt
segments.text: I am not against vegans. I am against being told about it before I have had coffee. With milk. From a friend.

segments.speaker: Linden Aldous
segments.text: And to the vegans listening, the rest of us are also exhausting. We talk about the barbecue like it is a religion. Fair is fair.

segments.speaker: Odessa Pruitt
segments.text: Last one. Dear Group Chat, a man with a mustache and a typewriter opened a store on my block that sells one candle and one plant. Is this a hipster?

segments.speaker: Linden Aldous
segments.text: That is not a hipster. That is a whole ecosystem. He also has a podcast about the candle.

segments.speaker: Odessa Pruitt
segments.text: Linden, you have a typewriter.

segments.speaker: Linden Aldous
segments.text: It is decorative, Odessa. I do not type on it. I just let people see it.

segments.speaker: Odessa Pruitt
segments.text: That is the most hipster sentence ever spoken on this station.

segments.speaker: Pat, the producer
segments.text: Letters may be edited for length. Pat edited them. Pat would like a raise.

segments.speaker: Linden Aldous
segments.text: It is quiz time. The game is called Billionaire or Bodega Cat.

segments.speaker: Odessa Pruitt
segments.text: I read a habit. You tell me if it belongs to a very rich man, or to Mister Biscuit, the cat at the deli on Lewis.

segments.speaker: Linden Aldous
segments.text: Our contestant is Tasha from Lewis, who knows Mister Biscuit personally.

segments.speaker: Tasha from Lewis
segments.text: I do. He owes me a dollar.

segments.speaker: Odessa Pruitt
segments.text: Question one. Renamed something everybody liked, to a single letter, and expected applause.

segments.speaker: Tasha from Lewis
segments.text: That is the billionaire. That is the Twitter man. Mister Biscuit would never. He respects a brand.

segments.speaker: Odessa Pruitt
segments.text: Correct. Elon Musk, one point. Question two. Has lived in the same house since the nineteen fifties and eats breakfast from a drive-through.

segments.speaker: Tasha from Lewis
segments.text: That sounds like Mister Biscuit. He has never moved. He eats whatever falls.

segments.speaker: Linden Aldous
segments.text: Wrong! That is Warren Buffett, one of the richest men alive, in Omaha. Same house. Same breakfast.

segments.speaker: Tasha from Lewis
segments.text: So the richest man in America lives like my grandfather. Respect.

segments.speaker: Odessa Pruitt
segments.text: Question three. Sits at the end of a very, very long table, so nobody can get close.

segments.speaker: Tasha from Lewis
segments.text: That is Mister Biscuit at the end of the counter. You cannot pet him. He decides.

segments.speaker: Linden Aldous
segments.text: Close, but no. That is Vladimir Putin. Famous for the long tables, the photos on a horse with no shirt, and elections he always seems to win.

segments.speaker: Tasha from Lewis
segments.text: Mister Biscuit has no shirt either, but at least he is a cat about it.

segments.speaker: Odessa Pruitt
segments.text: Question four. Changed his name to two letters, and the album release date moves like a bus schedule.

segments.speaker: Tasha from Lewis
segments.text: That is Kanye. Ye. He ran for president once. Mister Biscuit only ran for the door.

segments.speaker: Linden Aldous
segments.text: Correct. Question five. Is on television right now, in a rerun, somewhere, guaranteed.

segments.speaker: Tasha from Lewis
segments.text: Charlie Sheen. That sitcom never stops. I fell asleep in nineteen ninety nine and woke up, and it was still on.

segments.speaker: Odessa Pruitt
segments.text: Correct. They paid that man more per episode than this whole block makes in a year, and the reruns still pay the cable company.

segments.speaker: Linden Aldous
segments.text: Final question. Was let go on a Friday, came back within the week, and acted like nothing happened.

segments.speaker: Tasha from Lewis
segments.text: That is Mister Biscuit! They put him out every Friday, and every Monday he is back on the bread.

segments.speaker: Odessa Pruitt
segments.text: That is also Sam Altman. We are giving you both. The cat and the computer man.

segments.speaker: Linden Aldous
segments.text: Tasha, you win the grand prize. A dollar. From Mister Biscuit.

segments.speaker: Tasha from Lewis
segments.text: He still owes me the first one.

bits.title: Bunny Castellano, Live From the Problem

segments.speaker: Linden Aldous
segments.text: Let us go out to the street. Our reporter Bunny Castellano is live from the problem. Bunny?

segments.speaker: Bunny Castellano
segments.text: Linden! I am live at the corner of Fulton and Nostrand, where nobody has moved in four minutes, including me.

segments.speaker: Odessa Pruitt
segments.text: Bunny, what is the story?

segments.speaker: Bunny Castellano
segments.text: Odessa, the story is that it now costs money to drive into Manhattan below a certain street, and everybody in Brooklyn has an opinion, and I have heard all of them, today, from one man.

segments.speaker: Linden Aldous
segments.text: What does he think?

segments.speaker: Bunny Castellano
segments.text: He thinks it is terrible and also he takes the train. He just likes to be against things. He calls it cardio.

segments.speaker: Odessa Pruitt
segments.text: And the subway fare?

segments.speaker: Bunny Castellano
segments.text: The fare went up again. A woman told me the train is late, it smells like soup, and somehow it is still the best deal in the city.

segments.speaker: Linden Aldous
segments.text: She is right.

segments.speaker: Bunny Castellano
segments.text: She is always right. She has been riding the A train since before it had a letter.

segments.speaker: Odessa Pruitt
segments.text: Bunny, watch out for the e-bikes.

segments.speaker: Bunny Castellano
segments.text: Too late, Odessa. Three delivery bikes went by me on the sidewalk, one on the stairs, and one through a laundromat. I think he delivered to a dryer.

segments.speaker: Linden Aldous
segments.text: The apps keep promising the food in ten minutes.

segments.speaker: Bunny Castellano
segments.text: The food does come in ten minutes, Linden. The man brings it at the speed of a motorcycle on a bicycle lane, through a red light, with your soup in a bag held by his teeth. Tip him. He has seen things.

segments.speaker: Odessa Pruitt
segments.text: Where are you going next?

segments.speaker: Bunny Castellano
segments.text: To an office in Midtown, Odessa. My boss says we all have to return to the office.

segments.speaker: Linden Aldous
segments.text: What is at the office?

segments.speaker: Bunny Castellano
segments.text: Nothing, Linden. That is the scandal. There is one plant, a coffee machine that says maintenance, and a man in a quarter zip who keeps saying synergy to nobody.

segments.speaker: Odessa Pruitt
segments.text: So why go?

segments.speaker: Bunny Castellano
segments.text: Because somebody signed a very long lease on that office, Odessa, and now we are the furniture.

segments.speaker: Linden Aldous
segments.text: And the rent? Bunny, any news on the rent?

segments.speaker: Bunny Castellano
segments.text: I saw an apartment on the way. One bedroom, if you count the bed. The broker wanted a fee for opening the door. He did not open the door. It was already open.

segments.speaker: Odessa Pruitt
segments.text: Bunny Castellano, everybody, live from the problem.

segments.speaker: Bunny Castellano
segments.text: The problem is the whole city, Odessa. I love it here. Back to you.

bits.title: Generations, Apps and the Family Chat

segments.speaker: Odessa Pruitt
segments.text: Linden, I want to settle something. Which generation is the worst?

segments.speaker: Linden Aldous
segments.text: Odessa, that is a trap. Every generation is the worst to the one before it.

segments.speaker: Odessa Pruitt
segments.text: I am Gen X. We had no internet, no phones, and we came home when the streetlights came on. We raised ourselves.

segments.speaker: Linden Aldous
segments.text: And you still talk about it like you survived a war.

segments.speaker: Odessa Pruitt
segments.text: It was a war. It was a war against boredom, and we won it with a skateboard and a cassette.

segments.speaker: Linden Aldous
segments.text: Gen Z grew up with phones. They can edit a video before they can tie a shoe.

segments.speaker: Odessa Pruitt
segments.text: And they speak in a code. My niece said my outfit was giving. Giving what? She would not finish the sentence.

segments.speaker: Linden Aldous
segments.text: Giving is the whole sentence now, Odessa. Grammar has been optimized.

segments.speaker: Odessa Pruitt
segments.text: But Gen Z is kind, I will say. They talk about feelings. We did not have feelings. We had a chores list.

segments.speaker: Linden Aldous
segments.text: And then there is my generation, the millennials, stuck in the middle, who still own a printer and feel bad about it.

segments.speaker: Odessa Pruitt
segments.text: Now the apps. Each generation has its own app, like a church.

segments.speaker: Linden Aldous
segments.text: Facebook is for the aunties. Birthday wishes, a picture of a casserole, and a long post about a parking ticket from two thousand and twelve.

segments.speaker: Odessa Pruitt
segments.text: Facebook Marketplace, where every message is, is this still available, and then the person disappears forever.

segments.speaker: Linden Aldous
segments.text: Instagram is for the cousins. Everybody is on vacation, everybody is at brunch, and nobody's apartment looks like that.

segments.speaker: Odessa Pruitt
segments.text: Twitter is for men who want to argue with strangers about a movie at two in the morning.

segments.speaker: Linden Aldous
segments.text: It is called X now.

segments.speaker: Odessa Pruitt
segments.text: Nobody calls it that, Linden. Not even the men.

segments.speaker: Linden Aldous
segments.text: And WhatsApp is for the family. Fifty people, one uncle, and a good morning picture of a sunflower, every day, at five a m.

segments.speaker: Odessa Pruitt
segments.text: My mother sends the sunflower. I love the sunflower. Do not touch the sunflower.

segments.speaker: Linden Aldous
segments.text: So, men and women. Who uses the phone worse?

segments.speaker: Odessa Pruitt
segments.text: Men read one text, answer half of it, and think the conversation went well.

segments.speaker: Linden Aldous
segments.text: Women send four texts in a row, then one that says never mind, which is actually the most important one.

segments.speaker: Odessa Pruitt
segments.text: Linden, that one is true and I hate it.

segments.speaker: Linden Aldous
segments.text: So who is the worst generation?

segments.speaker: Odessa Pruitt
segments.text: The worst generation is whoever is holding the phone at the table. Put it down. Eat.

segments.speaker: Pat, the producer
segments.text: Pat is not on any of these apps. Pat is in the group chat. Pat is the group chat.

segments.speaker: Group Chat Jingle
segments.text: Tiny News. All the news that fits in a text.

segments.speaker: Tiny News
segments.text: Tiny News, read by Pat, who does not have opinions.

segments.speaker: Tiny News
segments.text: Abroad. Vladimir Putin was photographed again, at the far end of a long table. Experts say the table is now long enough to have its own weather.

segments.speaker: Tiny News
segments.text: In music. Ye, the artist formerly known as Kanye West, has a new album release date. Our sources say the date is a mood, not a day.

segments.speaker: Tiny News
segments.text: In television. A Charlie Sheen sitcom rerun is playing right now on at least one channel, as it has every hour since the early two thousands. The cable company thanks him.

segments.speaker: Tiny News
segments.text: In politics. The president's name was mentioned in a group chat on Halsey Street. Nine people left the chat. One stayed, to argue.

segments.speaker: Tiny News
segments.text: The mayor still wants free buses. A caller on Macon says this is why eggs cost money. A caller on Lewis says the mayor fixed her knee. Neither is true. Both called twice.

segments.speaker: Tiny News
segments.text: Markets. The stock market went up because a man on television said A I. Then it went down because a different man said it louder.

segments.speaker: Tiny News
segments.text: Crypto. Linden's cousin's coin is worth one sandwich today. Yesterday it was worth two sandwiches. Tomorrow, a napkin.

segments.speaker: Tiny News
segments.text: Transit. The G train was seen at a platform in Brooklyn this morning. Witnesses describe it as real, and brief.

segments.speaker: Tiny News
segments.text: Landmarks. Tourists at the Lady Verdigris asked a pigeon for directions. The pigeon said nothing, and walked away, and was right.

segments.speaker: Tiny News
segments.text: Nightlife. A techno party under the expressway ended at nine in the morning. Nobody smiled. Everyone says it was the best night of their lives.

segments.speaker: Tiny News
segments.text: Apps. The family WhatsApp on Monroe Street reached one thousand unread messages. The sunflower picture remains undefeated.

segments.speaker: Tiny News
segments.text: Weather. Marisol Gale says it is cold, and that she is taking it personally.

segments.speaker: Odessa Pruitt
segments.text: Pat, that was tiny and it was news. Thank you.

segments.speaker: Pat, the producer
segments.text: Thank you, Odessa. That is the news. I will log a request for more.

segments.speaker: Odessa Pruitt
segments.text: Now, a Group Chat tradition. Our own station impressionist, Rudy Falco, does his impression of Werner Herzog. Not the real one, obviously. Rudy just does a voice.

segments.speaker: Linden Aldous
segments.text: Rudy has never met him. Rudy has seen one documentary, on a bus.

segments.speaker: Odessa Pruitt
segments.text: Rudy, as the solemn director, welcome to Bed-Stuy. What do you see?

segments.speaker: Rudy Falco, impression
segments.text: I see a pigeon. He stands on the edge of the bodega awning. He has no plan. He has only the awning, and the awning has only him.

segments.speaker: Linden Aldous
segments.text: That is a normal pigeon, Rudy.

segments.speaker: Rudy Falco, impression
segments.text: There are no normal pigeons. There is only the pigeon, and the bagel he has stolen, and the long silence of the man who wanted that bagel.

segments.speaker: Odessa Pruitt
segments.text: Tell us about the bodega cat.

segments.speaker: Rudy Falco, impression
segments.text: The cat sleeps on the bread. He is the true owner of this store. The humans only work here. They ring up the lottery tickets, and the cat watches, and judges, and forgives nothing.

segments.speaker: Linden Aldous
segments.text: Rudy, it is alternate side parking day.

segments.speaker: Rudy Falco, impression
segments.text: Ah. The great migration. At eleven in the morning the men come down from the brownstones with their keys. They sit in their cars. They do not drive. They only wait, like monks of the curb.

segments.speaker: Odessa Pruitt
segments.text: That is accurate, actually.

segments.speaker: Rudy Falco, impression
segments.text: A man has waited ninety minutes to move his car eleven feet. I asked him why. His answer: the street sweeper is coming. The street sweeper did not come. The street sweeper never comes. We wait for it anyway. This is the human condition, with a ticket.

segments.speaker: Linden Aldous
segments.text: Rudy, try the dollar slice.

segments.speaker: Rudy Falco, impression
segments.text: The dollar slice is no longer one dollar. Nobody speaks of this. The sign still promises one dollar. The sign is a ghost. The cheese, however, is very much alive.

segments.speaker: Odessa Pruitt
segments.text: Any last words for our listeners?

segments.speaker: Rudy Falco, impression
segments.text: Go out onto your stoop. Look at the scaffolding. It has been there for nine years. It will outlive us all. Say goodnight to it, and to the pigeon.

segments.speaker: Linden Aldous
segments.text: Rudy, that was beautiful, and you are wearing a sweatshirt from a car wash.

segments.speaker: Odessa Pruitt
segments.text: That was Rudy Falco doing his impression of Werner Herzog. Not the real one, obviously. The real one has never heard of us.
